items.label: Theory
items.notes: Select one of the following series to be approved by the division chair. The courses must be completed with grades of C or better.

items.label: Public Recital
items.notes: Select 2 units from Music 163A through 163V (vocalists must also enroll in Music 161C as corequisite to 163V) taken in the primary performance area; students must consult and receive approval from the assigned music education faculty member before scheduling recital, which may be scheduled as early as fall quarter of the junior year.

nodes.title: Music Theory I
groups: Preparation for the Major: Music 20 Series
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours. Preparation: passing score on departmental examination. Course 20A is enforced Students must receive grade of C or better to proceed to next course in sequence. Theory: species counterpoint through fifth species; description of triads and inversions. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Music Theory II
groups: Preparation for the Major: Music 20 Series
nodes.prereq_text: course 20A with grade of C or better
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours. Theory: diatonic harmony through secondary dominants and diminished sevenths; modulations to dominant and relative keys; writing of four-part chorales; style composition in baroque dance forms; introduction to figured bass notation. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Music Theory III
groups: Preparation for the Major: Music 20 Series
nodes.prereq_text: course 20B with grade of C or better
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours. Theory: chromatic harmony including development of tonality, 1800 to 1850; appropriate analysis and style composition. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Project Approach to Music Theory I
groups: Preparation for the Major: Music 21 Series
nodes.prereq_text: passing score on departmental examination

requires.text: passing score on departmental examination

nodes.description: Lecture, four hours. Course 21A is enforced Students must receive grade of C or better to proceed to next course in sequence. Theory fundamentals through project approach. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Musicianship I
nodes.prereq_text: courses M6A, M6B, M6C
nodes.description: Laboratory, four hours. Course 102A is enforced Students must receive a grade of C- or better to proceed to next course in sequence. Advanced-level sight singing, sight reading, rhythm, melodic and harmonic dictation, tonal and modal improvisation, keyboard skills. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Musicianship II
nodes.prereq_text: courses M6A, M6B, M6C, 102A (102A with grade of C- or better)
nodes.description: Laboratory, four hours. Students must receive a grade of C- or better to proceed to next course in sequence. Advanced-level sight singing, sight reading, rhythm, melodic and harmonic dictation, tonal and modal improvisation, keyboard skills. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Musicianship III
nodes.prereq_text: courses M6A, M6B, M6C, 102A, 102B (102A, 102B with grades of C- or better)
nodes.description: Laboratory, four hours. Advanced-level sight singing, sight reading, rhythm, melodic and harmonic dictation, tonal and modal improvisation, keyboard skills. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Learning Approaches in Music Education
nodes.prereq_text: course 20A or 21A
nodes.description: Lecture, two hours; activity, two hours; outside study, eight hours. Introduction to music education by development of concepts, attitudes, and skills necessary to teach music and philosophical, historical, cultural, and psychological foundations of music education, with emphasis on learning theories and psychology of music learning. Contextualization of concepts by engaging in nonnotational modes of music learning, including systematic aural transmission and informal learning. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Musicality and Creativity in Childhood
nodes.description: Lecture, two hours; activity, two hours; outside study, eight hours. Preparation of music education students for teaching music at preschool and elementary school levels. Development of understanding of developmental characteristics, diverse cultures, and learning needs of children and design of effective instructional strategies that are age-appropriate and responsive to children’s background. Focus on practice of student-centered curriculum where students are active learners and teachers are facilitators to become proficient in providing children with music learning environment that is conducive to optimal growth in their musicality and creativity. Frequent field visits. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Comparative Study of Choral Music Education
nodes.description: Lecture, two hours; activity, one hour; fieldwork, one hour; outside study, eight hours. Preparation of students for teaching choral music at middle and high school levels. Development of understanding of developmental characteristics, diverse cultures, and learning needs of adolescents and design of effective instructional strategies that are age-appropriate and responsive to students’ background. Diverse practices and learning processes in choral music of American and world serve as basis of comparative study, with emphasis on comprehensive music education through performance. Frequent field visits. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Comparative Study of Instrumental Music Education
nodes.description: Lecture, two hours; activity, one hour; fieldwork, one hour; outside study, eight hours. Critical study and analysis of philosophy, history, organization, curriculum, and literature of music programs for elementary and secondary instrumental music instruction in traditional and nontraditional settings. Development of strategies and techniques to teach music in group settings. Completion of capstone project in form of electronic portfolio demonstrating mastery of program learning outcomes. Frequent field visits. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Music Theory through Improvisation
nodes.prereq_text: courses M6A, M6B, M6C, and 20A, 20B, and 20C, or 21A, 21B, and 21C
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours. Course 111A is enforced Students must receive grade of C or better to proceed to next course in sequence. Theory through improvisation, technology, and arranging for ensembles. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Music Creation and Analysis through Technology
nodes.prereq_text: courses M6A, M6B, M6C, 111A (111A with grade of C or better), and 20A, 20B, and 20C, or 21A, 21B, and 21C
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours. Students must receive grade of C or better to proceed to next course in sequence. Theory through improvisation, technology, and arranging for ensembles. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Arranging Music for Educational Settings
nodes.prereq_text: courses M6A, M6B, M6C, 111A, 111B (111A and 111B with grades of C or better), and 20A, 20B, and 20C, or 21A, 21B, and 21C
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours. Theory through improvisation, technology, and arranging for ensembles. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Study of Instrumental Techniques: High Strings
nodes.prereq_text: (course 20A) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Studio, three hours. Requisite or Applied studies in basic performance techniques and tutorial materials. May be repeated once for credit. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Study of Instrumental Techniques: Low Strings
nodes.prereq_text: (course 20A) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Studio, three hours. Requisite or Applied studies in basic performance techniques and tutorial materials. May be repeated once for credit. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Vocal Techniques for Music Education I
nodes.description: Studio, two hours; outside study, one hour. Introduction to basic vocal techniques, breath and body, vocal mechanism, health and care of voice, and instructional techniques. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Vocal Techniques for Music Education II
nodes.prereq_text: (course 114C) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Studio, two hours; outside study, one hour. Requisite or Introduction to art of teaching voice, focusing on vocal instruction in choral classroom. Focus on application of vocal techniques to choral music teaching at K-12 school settings. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Piano Skill in Classroom
nodes.description: Activity, two hours. Designed for Music Education majors. Development of piano skills and competencies that enable students to function successfully in general music, instrumental ensemble, and choral ensemble classrooms. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Study of Instrumental Techniques: Woodwinds
nodes.description: Studio, four hours; outside study, two hours. Applied studies in basic performance techniques and tutorial materials designed to give music education students knowledge to teach basic instrument concepts. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Study of Instrumental Techniques: Brass
nodes.description: Studio, four hours; outside study, two hours. Applied studies in basic performance techniques and tutorial materials designed to give music education students knowledge to teach basic instrument concepts. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Study of Instrumental Techniques: Percussion
nodes.description: Studio, four hours; outside study, two hours. Applied studies in basic performance techniques and tutorial materials designed to give music education students knowledge to teach basic instrument concepts. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Conducting
nodes.prereq_text: courses 20A, 20B, 20C, 120A
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours. Fundamentals of conducting, including basic skills, techniques, analysis, and repertoire. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Study and Conducting of Instrumental and Choral Literature
nodes.prereq_text: course 116
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours. Study and practice of conducting both instrumental and choral repertoire. In addition to further development of conducting gestures, focus on score study techniques, rehearsal techniques, style, and interpretation as applied to choral and instrumental repertoire. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Music Theory IV
nodes.prereq_text: course 20C with grade of C (2.0) or better
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, four hours. Preparation: passing score on departmental first-year examination. Theory: baroque counterpoint including chorale prelude; two-part invention; exposition and first modulation of three-part invention; canonic principles; analysis of inventions, canons, and fugues. Musicianship: sight-singing of extended chromatic melodies; advanced harmonic dictation (diatonic and chromatic); keyboard harmonization of modulating melodies; elementary score reading. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Music Theory V
nodes.prereq_text: course 120A with grade of C (2.0) or better
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, four hours. Theory: advanced chromatic harmony including development of harmony from 1850; analytical projects; style composition. Musicianship: advanced score reading; advanced harmonic dictation; preparation for departmental examination. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Music Theory VI
nodes.prereq_text: course 120B with grade of C (2.0) or better
nodes.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, two hours; listening, two hours. 20th-century harmonic language, including nonfunctional harmony, polytonality, free atonality, serialism, and minimalism. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Symphonic Band
groups: Preparation for the Major: Large Conducted Ensembles
nodes.description: Activity, two hours. Preparation: audition. Group performance of instrumental music scored for band. May be repeated for credit without limitation. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Marching and Varsity Bands
groups: Preparation for the Major: Large Conducted Ensembles
nodes.description: Activity, six hours. Preparation: audition. Group performance of special band arrangements for football and basketball games as well as special events. May be repeated for credit without limitation. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: UCLA Chorale
groups: Preparation for the Major: Large Conducted Ensembles
nodes.description: Activity, four hours. Preparation: audition. Large mixed ensemble performing choral music of all periods appropriate for concert choral ensemble. May be repeated for credit without limitation. May be concurrently scheduled with course C480A. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Chamber Singers
groups: Preparation for the Major: Large Conducted Ensembles
nodes.description: Activity, four hours. Preparation: audition. Designed primarily for Music Performance majors. Select mixed ensemble performing chamber choral music of all periods. May be repeated for credit without limitation. May be concurrently scheduled with course C480B. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Opera Workshop
groups: Preparation for the Major: Large Conducted Ensembles
nodes.description: Activity, six hours. Preparation: audition. Rehearsal and performance of scenes and complete operas, as well as repertoire, stage movement, and foreign language diction coaching. May be repeated for credit without limitation. May be concurrently scheduled with course C480C. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Symphony Orchestra
groups: Preparation for the Major: Large Conducted Ensembles
nodes.description: Activity, three hours. Preparation: audition. Group performance of symphonic orchestral literature. May be repeated for credit without limitation. May be concurrently scheduled with course C480D. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Philharmonia
groups: Preparation for the Major: Large Conducted Ensembles
nodes.description: Activity, six hours. Preparation: audition. Designed primarily for Music Performance majors. Group performance of symphonic orchestral literature, as well as orchestral accompaniment for operatic and major choral works. May be repeated for credit without limitation. May be concurrently scheduled with course C480E. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Wind Ensemble
groups: Preparation for the Major: Large Conducted Ensembles
nodes.description: Activity, six hours. Preparation: audition. Group performance of concert literature for wind ensemble. May be repeated for credit without limitation. May be concurrently scheduled with course C480G. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Global Musicianship
nodes.description: (Same as Ethnomusicology M6A and Musicology M6A.) Laboratory, four hours. Course M6A is enforced Students must receive grade of C– or better to proceed to next course in sequence. Introduction to global musicianship through in-depth exploration of basic musical elements through performance, aural skills, and active listening. Engages with melodic information represented in solfège, harmonic information in Nashville number system, and rhythmic information in both Western notation and digital audio workstation grid visualization. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Musicianship
nodes.prereq_text: course M6A with grade of C– or better
nodes.description: (Same as Ethnomusicology M6B and Musicology M6B.) Laboratory, four hours. Preparation: placement examination. Introduction to musicianship through in-depth exploration of basic common musical elements and training in aural recognition, sight singing, dictation, and keyboard skills. Focus on topics such as tonal and modal harmony, rhythm, improvisation, composition, notation, and ear training to prepare students for later theory courses, participation in music ensembles, advanced study in music, and professional careers. Letter grading.
